[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-16e[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Self-healing agent workspace preparation[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]A new SASE agent launch into a numbered ephemeral workspace never [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]fails because of state an earlier run left behind (unpublishable [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]sidecar commits, merge/rebase conflicts, in-progress git [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]operations, dirty or diverged checkouts). Old state is rescued [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]durably outside the workspace on a best-effort basis, the workspace[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]is healed or re-created from the primary checkout, and the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]bead-merge bug that triggered the original failure is fixed at its [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]root.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]6[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]3[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Durable rescue store and non-refusing sidecar eviction[/bold #D7AFFF]        [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]rescue-store[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]rescue-store: add a best-effort rescue store outside the workspace (git [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]bundles, worktree patches, manifests, retention, one notification per [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]rescue) and change launch-time sidecar protection to publish once, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]rescue, and always proceed with eviction instead of raising [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]_WorkspaceBeadEvictionRefused.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Self-healing checkout preparation for numbered workspaces[/bold #D7AFFF]     [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]checkout-heal[dim] · [dim][/dim]after rescue-store[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]checkout-heal: give prepare_workspace an opt-in self-heal ladder for [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]numbered workspaces that rescues state, aborts in-progress git [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]operations, survives stash failures, replaces a conflicting sync rebase [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]with rescue plus hard reset to the default branch, and verifies a clean [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]postcondition.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Last-resort workspace re-creation and non-holding setup [/bold #D7AFFF]      [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]failures[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]reclone[dim] · [dim][/dim]after checkout-heal[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]reclone: when in-place healing still fails, rescue and move the numbered[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]checkout aside, re-materialize it from the primary checkout, chdir into [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]it, and prepare it once more (launch, retry, and linked-repo paths); [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]release rather than hold workspaces whose setup ultimately failed.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Order-preserving bead event stream merge in sase-core[/bold #D7AFFF]         [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]core-merge[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]core-merge: in the sase-core repo, stop the bead event-stream merge from[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]re-sorting already-published upstream events by timestamp, and accept [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pure-reorder branches produced by the old merge so wedged clones can [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]heal.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Bead sync rollback and wedged-clone healing[/bold #D7AFFF]                   [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]bead-sync[dim] · [dim][/dim]after core-merge[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]bead-sync: bump the sase-core pin, roll a clone back when the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]post-integration stream guard rejects an integration, abort cleanly on [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]deadline timeouts, and mirror the pure-reorder tolerance in the Python [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]stream-integrity guard.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  6 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Truthful setup-failure reporting[/bold #D7AFFF]                              [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]

    [#D7D7AF]stdout line-buffered so the output file interleaves stdout/stderr [/#D7D7AF]
